Grace is vexed when she learns that Leo's ex-girlfriend (Mira Sorvino) is intimately acquainted with Will.
Karen invites Grace and Leo to play tennis at her exclusive club, but her fierce playing style drives Grace away.
Jack lands a speaking role opposite James Earl Jones in an off-Broadway play and gives the veteran actor some pointers.
Will takes Leo on shopping sprees and for high tea to help him rekindle his love of the city; Karen coaches Jack for the annual gay spelling bee.
Will takes his mother for an afternoon stroll and bumps into an attractive bachelor (Dylan McDermott); Karen continues her lifelong quest to hunt down hubby-stealing Lorraine.
An unorthodox doctor (Jack Black) gives Karen her annual physical; Jack begs Will to support his decision to become a student nurse.
Will urges Grace to stay in New York so they can spend some time together; Karen strong-arms Jack's nursing teacher into letting him skip class but still make the grade.
Will catches the eye of a female diner after being stood up; Grace bumps into a man (Tom Everett Scott) with whom she once shared a forgettable encounter; Karen runs into her nemesis, Candice Bergen.

A weak bladder forces Will to entrust Grace with his place in line for Barry Manilow tickets; Grace's mother (Debbie Reynolds) cancels their annual mother-daughter shopping trip to have dinner with Jack.

Grace's freeloading sister (Geena Davis) comes to town to launch her latest business enterprise; Karen spurns Lyle (John Cleese), then changes her mind after Lorraine (Minnie Driver) expresses her disapproval.
A rich plastic surgeon (guest star Hal Linden) tries to buy Will's affection; Grace boycotts a new restaurant.
Will's new client (Dave Foley) falls for Jack; Grace and Karen discover hidden money while trying to fix the plumbing in Leo's cabin.
Will is the only single man in a cooking class full of couples, including Jack and his new boyfriend (Dave Foley); Karen's mother (Suzanne Pleshette) asks Grace to decorate her apartment.
Will and Grace begin a business venture selling apartments; Jack runs into his former acting mentor, Zandra; Karen and Lyle (John Cleese) try to renew romance.
Will and Grace try to break up Jack and Stuart (Dave Foley) so they can sell the apartment for a higher price; Karen demands that Lyle (John Cleese) discipline his daughter (Minnie Driver).
Real estate entrepreneurs Will and Grace face formidable competition on the East Side from a lesbian couple (Edie Falco, Chloë Sevigny); John Edward gives Karen some psychic guidance.
Jack and Grace stumble upon Stuart (Dave Foley) watching a movie matinée in the company of another man; Will tries to teach Karen how to drive.
Zack's father falls for Miss Bliss.
Screech finds that an intimidating student has a learning disability.
Zack and a classmate ask the same girl to an upcoming dance, jeopardizing their friendship.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) scheme to get more time to study for a midterm ends up hurting his teacher. With Dennis Haskins.
A student argument helps a teacher resolve a problem with a longtime friend. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
A teacher turns a practical joke into a lesson about the criminal justice system. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to steal a kiss from a returning former student who is now a famous rock star.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is offered a chance to join a popular club. With Dustin Diamond.
A retired teacher with unorthodox methods stimulates the class when he substitutes for their regular teacher.
The gang enters a dance contest being held at the Max and hosted by radio personality Casey Kasem. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Lisa's (Lark Voorhies) friends invent ways to pay the bills she has accrued on her father's credit card. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
A freak lightning accident enables Screech (Dustin Diamond) to predict the future. With Tiffani-Amber Thiessen and Mario Lopez.
The guys hide a microphone at the girls' party to find out whom Kelly will ask to the dance.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) gets into unusual circumstances and clothes when he tries to help Screech (Dustin Diamond) get a date.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plan to get rid of Slater (Mario Lopez) backfires; Slater's revenge ends up benefiting Screech (Dustin Diamond).
When Ms. Simpson injures her back, a substitute teacher named Tony Crane takes over her class at Bayside; when all the girls fall for Mr. Crane, Zack and Slater become jealous.
When Kelly is nominated as homecoming queen, her dream is shattered as she faces the prospect of winning after she gets a zit; Zack comes up with a solution, but it does not unfold as he plans.
Zack bets against a Valley wrestler named Marvin Nedick that Slater will win his wrestling match against Nedick; things go wrong when Slater decides to quit wrestling.
In order for Kelly to go to a George Michael concert, she has to pass her science test. Zack persuades Screech to tutor Kelly, a ploy which is more for his benefit than for Kelly's.
Zack and his friends form a company selling friendship bracelets for a business class project. He names himself as boss, but Kelly, Jessie, and Slater feel he is treating them poorly.
Everyone is put into pairs for a class assignment to act out married life, so they can be prepared for marriage as adults.
Jessie and Zack (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar) run for student president, each for different reasons.
Zack's use of a subliminal tape to get Kelly to fall for him has results he never intended.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to get Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to be his girl land him in detention with a rival for her affections.
The pranks between rival schools Bayside and Valley escalate during the week of the city cheerleading finals.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) alien disguise is so believable it attracts a government UFO investigator.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) decides to throw a surprise birthday party for Screech (Dustin Diamond) in the principal's office.
Slater's (Mario Lopez) pet dies while in Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) care.
Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) chooses to go to the prom with Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar); Lisa and Screech (Lark Voorhies, Dustin Diamond) have a "trial" date.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes a leader of men when he joins a cadet corps to get out of detention.
The gang uses an old radio station in the school basement to hold a marathon. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's antics get Slater thrown out of driver education classes.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) house party turns into a disaster when his mother's favorite statue is broken. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to cope when he ends up with two dates for the same night; Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) agrees to a blind date.
Zack has a waiter impersonate his father for a meeting with the principal.
The Miss Bayside Beauty Pageant attracts unusual contestants; Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) make a bet.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) becomes addicted to caffeine pills as she strives to be a perfect student. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) "Girls of Bayside" calendar catches the eye of a fashion photographer. With Dustin Diamond.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) advice line backfires and gets him into trouble with everyone. With Mario Lopez.

Zack makes a surprising discovery about his Native American heritage; Lisa learns her family tree includes a Black American hero of the Underground Railroad; Jessie grapples with guilt over her slave-trading ancestry.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) asks Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to go steady and then falls in love with the school nurse.
Mr. Belding's brother Rod (guest star Edward Blatchford) scores points with the class as a substitute history teacher. With Dennis Haskins and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.
Panic hits when Screech (Dustin Diamond) finds out he has to play a Russian exchange student in the chess finals. With Dennis Haskins.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).
Eric tries to blackmail Slater (Mario Lopez) and learns a disturbing truth about his date with Lisa (Lark Voorhies).
The student council decides to hold a dance-date auction to raise money for new cheerleading uniforms.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) needs a high SAT score to achieve her dream of attending prestigious Stansbury University.
When a girl isn't allowed to try out for the wrestling team, the students band together and protest the decision.
Teenage movie star Johnny Dakota chooses Bayside as the site for an anti-drug commercial. With Mario Lopez and Dustin Diamond.
On Bayside's annual "cut school day," Mr. Belding warns Zack that if he is absent one more time he will be suspended.
Lisa and Screech make a "love machine" for their science project.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) latest moneymaking scheme involves a "Girls of Bayside" video-dating tape.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) does everything in her power to break up her father's wedding. With Dustin Diamond.
Everyone gets summer jobs at a fancy beach club and decides to hold Zack's birthday party there.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) promises Mr. Carosi (Ernie Sabella) the gang will win a volleyball game against a rival beach club.
Stacy (Leah Remini) gets confused after she enters a contest at Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) urging and finds that he voted for Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen).
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is in love with Stacy (Leah Remini) but fears she is only interested in her college boyfriend.
Stacy (Leah Remini), in charge of the club for the day, learns her father booked two parties for the same night. With Mario Lopez.
Stacy (Leah Remini) moves out after her father forbids her to see Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar).
The entire gang goes to the mall to obtain U2 tickets and ends up camping out overnight. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
Jessie's father invites everyone to his Palm Springs resort to attend his wedding. With Elizabeth Berkley and Mario Lopez.
Casey Kasem (guest starring as himself) chronicles the rise of the rock group Zack Attack. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
The students are shocked during the Christmas season to discover the new girl working in Mr. Moody's store is homeless.
Zack's family invites Laura and her father home for Christmas.
Lisa (Lark Voorhies) wins a mystery weekend at Mr. Jameson's mansion and invites the gang to participate. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
A staycation for Paddy, Freddie and Chris, as they drive British grand tourers on Wales's roads; Chris Harris pays tribute to Sir Stirling Moss and his battles against Ferrari.
An all-electric, all-terrain ice cream van that sweeps streets and has an on-board rubber ring for aquatic delivery.

A compilation of the fastest cars; Chris Harris heads to Italy to test the Ferrari SF90; the team test the battery operated Honda E, Vauxhall Corsa E and Mini electric; a tribute to the late Sir Sterling Moss.
Freddie, Chris and Paddy head to the Lake District for an emotional reunion with their own dads' old cars; Chris heads out on track to test Lamborghini's most powerful car ever, the hybrid Sian.
The team try out some of James Bond's greatest cars, including the legendary Aston Martin DB5.
Freddie, Chris and Paddy head on an icy expedition across the wild Scottish Highlands in the new Land Rover Defender, Mercedes G-Wagen and Ariel Nomad.

Freddie, Chris and Paddy confront the male midlife crisis by buying the perfect sports cars for "gentlemen of a certain age;" back at the track, Chris tests out the raucous new Toyota GR Yaris hot hatch.
Team Top Gear is up against the Florida locals in events including donk-car drag racing, a swamp buggy shoot-out, all ending up at the Freedom Factory Raceway for a NASCAR-style showdown.
On a mission to give the trundling trailblazer Sinclair one more eccentric adventure, Fred attempts to break the national speed limit whilst piloting the C5 down an Olympic bobsleigh run.
Chris, Freddie, and Paddy decide to get their lorry licenses, and become fully fledged HGV drivers themselves.

The team finds out if it is possible to get a reliable used car for less than £500; Chris lives the high life in Maserati's new MC20 supercar, while Freddie goes on the charge in the all-electric Rivian pick-up truck.
Freddie, Chris, and Paddy celebrate 100 years of the BBC by tackling motorsport 1920s-style.

America loves pick-up trucks, but there's a country even more obsessed with them than the U.S., and that's Thailand; Chris Harris tests the Rimac Nevera, a 2,000 horsepower all-electric car from Croatia.
The hosts set out to build a bridge over the River Kwai in Thailand, but must first drive across Burma.
Jeremy Clarkson takes the Kia Cee'd on a road test; a game of rugby with James May.
The trio treks to Ukraine in a Volkswagen Up, a Ford Fiesta and a Dacia Sandero; James Blunt in the "Reasonably Priced Car."
Jeremy Clarkson races the Jaguar XJ against the rotation of the Earth itself.
The Supercar Shootout in Italy with the Lamborghini Aventador, the McLaren MP4-12C and the Noble M6000, guest will.i.am.
China's ever-expanding car industry; NASCAR racing, guest Matt LeBlanc.
When talking about supercars, it tends to be all about their big numbers, power, speed and cost; the presenters believe that supercars shouldn't just be about boring, bare numbers.
Fearless Fred Flintoff attempts F1 Stock Car Racing; Chris Harris gets a call offering a Mercedes-AMG One test drive.
Young, inexperienced drivers and mechanics have a shot at the big time; following how they cope when pitted against well-funded drivers who've been doing it for years.
Chris, Freddie and Paddy deploy science to find the best family car you can buy.
Featuring Smart Roadster.
Jeremy and his '69 Mercedes Grosser go up against James and his '72 Rolls-Royce in a series of routine driving tasks.
Bad cars; Ford Mustang; David Soul.
Tribute to Jaguar; Boris Johnson is "The Star in a Reasonably Priced Car."
Porsche 911; TR6; Anne Robinson is "The Star in a Reasonably Priced Car".
Jim investigates killing during robbery.
Hardie goes undercover to the town of Alder Gulch to investigate stagecoach robberies.

Jim is sent to Moose Creek, Canada, to identify the corpse of an outlaw only he has seen, but the man was killed with a shotgun blast to the face, which makes him hard to identify; a woman claims the body is her brother's body.
The son of a dead man accused of a stage coach robbery finds an empty strongbox in the attic and hopes that Jim Hardie can help him uncover the real thieves.
Hardie gives a job to the son of a former employee who was fired.
Hardie tries to prevent a lynching when a town's hard cases accuse a Basque sheepherder of the abduction of a young girl.
Jim goes undercover as a trainee for Wells Fargo, to try and find out who is supplying renegade Indians with the guns they are using on their murderous raids.
Hardie isn't pleased when a man and beautiful woman insist on becoming passengers on the stagecoach he will use.
Jim Hardie is ordered to infiltrate Sam Bass' gang so that he can learn where they hole up between raids.
Jim Hardie is called in to investigate what happened to a long overdue stagecoach; among passengers were the son of a wealthy rancher and his fiancée.
Jim Hardie joins a group of passengers aboard a stagecoach that includes a woman and her son, a reporter and an outlaw.
When Jesse James and his gang are suspected of robbing a bank in Missouri, Jim Hardie goes undercover to try to find the outlaw.
Hardie is called to investigate when a Wells Fargo agent dies and a large sum of money is determined to be missing from the man's office.
Outlaw Belle Starr and her gang rob a train on which Jim Hardie is a passenger, and he tries to lure her from hiding by tempting her with a prominent racehorse.

A rookie outlaw holds up the stage carrying cash that Jim is waiting for, prompting Jim to go off looking for the thief, but he finds he needs the criminal's help when the two must evade an Indian attack.
Jim joins a father who's searching for his missing son in the Superstition Mountains -- an area held sacred by the Apaches.
As the only witness to a robbery, Hardie is targeted by the robber's partner.
A woman must protect herself and her daughter from a callous man.
A gang joins the train in the guise of farmers and plans to take it over.
While in the desert, Cooper finds a prospector who is lost and near death from exposure and thirst.
While traveling with Chris Hale's wagon train, a young woman (Laraine Day) with a criminal past is blamed for the theft of a passenger's money.
An Army deserter turns himself in to leaders of the wagon train.
Disguised as a layman, a troubled priest (Michael Parks) joins Chris Hale's wagon train in an attempt to forget his past. Guest star: Dick York.
A newspaper man and two ex-convicts plan to expose a lawman as a wanted train robber.
A frightened emigrant destroys the last of the food supplies on the train.

When he plans to ride shotgun on a stage carrying a bank shipment, Jess is asked to look the other way and allow a robbery, but when Jess tries to have the man arrested, the office manager refuses to press charges.
Jess finds remains of a U.S. Army wagon that disappeared during the war that contained $60,000 in gold.
Slim and Jess try to help a mysterious stranger who's been hiding in the mountains, killing Sherman cattle and leaving gold pieces to pay for the animals.
Jess is critically wounded when he tries to warn Marshal McGarry, who is transporting a prisoner to hang, that the prisoner's brother plans to attack the tumbleweed wagon.
Slim finds an injured young woman, only to be mistaken for one of her kidnappers when her father finds them.
Jim goes on the hunt for a band of robbers that is targeting Pony Express riders.
Jim Hardie is sent to negotiate a right of way for their stagecoaches through Sam Brundage's property.
Hardie investigates a stagecoach holdup where white men disguised as Indians kill the driver and the guard and leave a lady for dead.
At the Wells Fargo auction, a man and a woman bid vigorously on a destroyed suitcase.
Hardie is sent in when a stagecoach is robbed near the Arizona-New Mexico border, and he learns that the only thing taken was a scrappy dog whose collar may be evidence to prove a murder.
Jim Hardie and his Wells Fargo agents set a trap for the notorious Stillwell gang, but the outlaws manage to outwit the detectives and escape with five thousand dollars.
Jim Hardie tries to clear a colleague of a murder charge after the man is found standing over a dead man, holding a smoking gun.
The Wells Fargo team is tasked with protecting a shipment of jade in San Francisco.
Hardie rides with a bigoted general on a mission to quell a Sioux uprising.
Hardie spends Christmas hunting for gunrunners moving weapons across the Mexican border.
An old friend of Jim Hardie's is killed in a Wells Fargo express office robbery.
Hardie tries to find a prisoner's hidden loot.
Jim protects a woman who is a material witness in a San Francisco corruption investigation.
A man (Everett Sloane) suspects his cook (Beulah Bondi) of being an arsenic-poisoning murderer. With Janet Ward.
A down-on-his-luck man responds to a newspaper ad from a man seeking a companion for a cross-country trip.
A man (Tom Ewell) believes an exact double is gradually taking over his life.
A woman (Judith Evelyn) is suspected of murdering her husband, who has been having an affair with another woman. With Joe Mantell and Kathleen McGuire.
A larcenous store Santa (Barry Fitzgerald) helps change the ways of a potential delinquent (Bobby Clark).
A man (Darren McGavin) tries to trick an elderly woman (Patricia Collinge) out of a family heirloom.
A man (John Qualen) is surprised to learn that the boss he thought he had murdered is still alive. With Philip Reed.
A gunman (George Mathews), intent on murdering his girlfriend, purchases an alibi.
An escaped convict (John Cassavetes) takes refuge in a farmhouse occupied by a young housewife (Marisa Pavan).
A year after the murders, a newspaper reporter (Joan Lorring) attempts to interview Lizzie Borden (Carmen Mathews) and her sister about the killings.
A bum (Robert Newton) witnesses a murder and decide to take advantage of the situation. With Philip Reed.
A police detective (Charles Bronson) investigating a murder focuses on a strange ventriloquist (Claude Rains).
A female reporter (Claire Trevor) encounters problem trying to leave Eastern Europe after meeting a soccer star.
A man (Mark Damon) arrives at a monastery bent on revenge and is convinced by a kind priest (Everett Sloane) to mend his heart.
An English man (John Williams) murders his wife and moves to California, thinking he has committed the perfect crime.
Two greedy brothers plan to murder their elderly aunt (Mildred Natwick) in an attempt to inherit her money.
A desperate couple (Charles Bronson, Norma Crane) plans to rob an eccentric old woman (Estelle Winwood).
An angel (Alan Napier) allows a murdered mystery writer (John Williams) to return to Earth to uncover his killer.
An unemployed man (John Qualen) needing money is hired by an unknown employer (Lorne Greene) to commit murder.
A man (Philip Abbott) is startled to see a portrait of his first wife four years after she disappeared.
An antiques dealer (Robert H. Harris) decides his art objects are too beautiful to sell. With Louise Larabee.
An insecure woman (Phyllis Thaxter) who can't control her drinking loses control at a cocktail party.
Using a haunted house in their ploy, two men (Ralph Clanton, John Irving) scheme to con a wealthy American (Biff McGuire) out of his money.
A garrulous babysitter (Thelma Ritter) enjoys being the center of attention after her employer is murdered.
A murderer (Jack Mullaney) hides from a posse after killing a school teacher's (Pat Hitchcock) fiancé.
A man (Biff McGuire) struggles to remember the license plate number of the vehicle that killed his fiancée (Judith Ames).
While vacationing in Palm Beach, a reserved heiress (Leora Dana) becomes the romantic focus of a prince (Jacques Bergerac).
A woman (Ruth Hussey) is stunned to learn that a mink coat she bought had been stolen from a previous owner.
An executive (Howard Duff) plans to end an associate's (Dan Dailey) love affair and save the man's career and marriage.
A suspicious sergeant (William Conrad) digs when a death is labeled accidental. With David Wayne.
A woman (Anne Francis) stands trial for her husband's murder, and the family maid (Ruth Roman) holds the key to the truth.
A woman (Inger Stevens) thinks her refusal of the use of her phone led to a murder. With Dan O'Herlihy.
A girl's (Zohra Lampert) deep love for a compulsive thief (Robert Redford) infuriates his jealous accomplice (Barry Morse).
When a young couple moves into a new neighborhood, they find their lives threatened by the little boy next door.
A man (Gary Merrill) must stop his wife (Joan Fontaine) from alienating family and friends.
The relatives (Ed Nelson, Sarah Marshall) of a murdered newlywed decide to bring the killer to justice. With Peter Graves.
A young pianist (Robert Horton) is framed, by the woman (Cara Williams) he loves, for a murder he did not commit.
A New York City woman (Constance Ford) is convinced she will be the next victim of a serial killer. With Steve Brodie.
Murder results when a wife (Joanne Woodward) nags her husband (Skip Homeier) to stand up for himself.
After his daughter commits murder, a man (Sir Cedric Hardwicke) finds a way to protect his family's reputation.
An escaped mental patient (George Grizzard) encounters a woman (Phyllis Thaxter) who's afraid to be alone in her house.
Two friends unknowingly tell a middle-aged professor (Robert Emhardt) about his wife's (Cara Williams) reputation.
A brother and sister (Hume Cronyn, Carmen Mathews) scheme to defraud an insurance company. With James Gleason.
A man (Hurd Hatfield) assumes another identity to kill his aunt (Mildred Dunnock) but forgets one important detail.
A man (Robert H. Harris) is overjoyed to learn that his long-forsaken love (Jessica Tandy) has searched him out to marry him.
A murderer (Lee Philips) searches for an alibi after he kills a rival gangster (Chick Chandler) in a fit of rage.
Two sisters (Dorothy Stickney, Carmen Mathews) resort to desperate measures to keep their house.
A man (Robert Horton) stakes his job, home and life savings on the turn of a card. With Robert Middleton.
A young man is overcome with grief when he learns of his father's demise and accuses his new mother of the crime.
An underworld kingpin (Robert Middleton) learns that his wife (Kathleen Hughes) has been unfaithful to him. With Henry Silva.
A publisher (John Williams), intrigued by an unpublished murder mystery, visits the author (Patricia Collinge).
A mystery writer with an overactive imagination conjures up murderous thoughts about her new neighbors.
A wife (Leora Dana) regrets having her sane husband (Russell Collins) committed to a mental institution.
Newlyweds (Biff McGuire, Mary Scott) meet a volatile stranger (Robert Emhardt) while on their honeymoon.
A gorgeous actress (Barbara Baxley) asks a neighbor (Henry Jones) to help her hide the body of a murder victim.
A man (Harry Townes) kills a gubernatorial candidate to ensure his brother's (Royal Dano) election. With Inger Stevens.
A prisoner tries to convince a police sergeant to allow him to escape while they are on their way to San Quentin.
A man tries one last desperate attempt to win back the woman he loves by inviting her new lover for a drink.
